definitions.explanation: The color green, as seen in leaves and grass.

examples.japanese: {緑色|みどりいろ}の{葉|は}が{美|うつく}しい。
{信号|しんごう}が{緑色|みどりいろ}に{変|か}わった。
examples.english: The traffic light changed to green.

examples.japanese: この{絵|え}の{具|ぐ}は{緑色|みどりいろ}が{鮮|あざ}やかだ。
examples.english: This paint has a vivid green.

examples.japanese: {春|はる}になると、{山|やま}が{緑色|みどりいろ}に{染|そ}まる。
examples.english: In spring, the mountains are dyed green.

notes:
{緑|みどり} (green) + {色|いろ} (color). The explicit color-name form, used when specifying or describing the color green precisely.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {緑色|みどりいろ}の{野菜|やさい}: green vegetables
- {緑色|みどりいろ}に{光|ひか}る: to shine green
- {緑色|みどりいろ}に{染|そ}まる: to be dyed green
- {濃|こ}い{緑色|みどりいろ}: dark green
- {薄|うす}い{緑色|みどりいろ}: light green

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {緑|みどり}: green — used more broadly and poetically; {緑色|みどりいろ} is more concrete and descriptive
- {青|あお}: blue/green — traditionally covers both blue and green in Japanese; traffic lights are called {青|あお} even though they appear green

USAGE:
In Japanese, {青|あお} historically encompassed both blue and green. The distinction between {青|あお} and {緑|みどり} became clearer in modern Japanese, but {青|あお} is still used for green traffic lights and green apples ({青|あお}りんご). {緑色|みどりいろ} is unambiguously green.
